public_rationale: Marcus said he does not expect LeCun's world-model approach to solve many of the problems that have plagued LLMs. The source post names that approach as JEPA. He gave no deadline. According to a summary dated April 2026, LeCun left Meta in November 2025 to build a company focused on world models. The summary says that company, AMI Labs, is meant to remain a research organisation and is not expected to produce a saleable product for around five years (e1). The evidence gathered contains no public evaluation of AMI Labs or JEPA-based systems on known LLM problems such as hallucination, reasoning reliability or generalization. It also does not show either event that would settle the forecast early. One is evaluations showing a JEPA-based system clearly solving several of those problems. The other is the company abandoning the approach. With no results so far, the forecast can be neither confirmed nor contradicted.
limitations: The evidence is a single secondary summary (e1) about AMI Labs' status and plans. It contains no technical results.
'Many of the problems' is not quantified, so later evidence may also be hard to score.
Marcus phrased this as an expectation, not a firm prediction.
